title: Times tables
summary: Learn the times tables with pictures and practise them in a short game: 2, 5 and 10 first, then 0 and 1, then the rest up to 12 × 12.
guide: 3 × 4 means 3 rows of 4. That is why every fact comes with a picture: rows of little dots. If you forget a fact, count the dots or go down row by row: 4, 8, 12.
You can also say a {{term:multiplication-table}} out loud, in order: "one five is five, two fives are ten, three fives are fifteen…". Each time, one more row of 5 joins the picture.
Type your answer with the number buttons and press ✓. If it is wrong, that's fine: look at the picture and try again. That fact will come back a few questions later so it sticks.
Facts you get wrong are remembered on this device only, and come back first next time. Nothing is sent over the internet.
The ⏱ button turns on a gentle timer (6 seconds, like the Year 4 multiplication check). If time runs out, your answer is not marked wrong; we just practise that fact more. Leave it off if you prefer.

engine.label-retype: Look at the picture and try again.
engine.label-recite-done: You said the whole table! {n} of {t} right first time.
engine.label-fb-zero: Anything times zero is zero: there is nothing to count.
engine.label-fb-one: Times 1 leaves a number the same.
engine.label-fb-add: You added {a} and {b}. Times means {a} rows of {b}.
engine.label-fb-near: So close! It looks like one row or one column too many or too few.
engine.label-fb-off-one: So close! You are one out.

say-five-table.title: Say the 5 times table
say-five-table.prompt: Say the 5 times table in order and type each answer: 1 × 5, 2 × 5, 3 × 5… Each time, a new row of 5 joins the picture.
say-five-table.hint: Look at the number at the end of each row: 5, 10, 15… Each answer is 5 more than the one before.
say-five-table.success: Well done! You said the 5 times table.
say-five-table.why: Why is each answer in the 5 times table exactly 5 more than the one before?
say-five-table.model: Because each step adds one more row of 5 to the picture. 4 × 5 is 4 rows of 5, and 5 × 5 has one more row of 5, so it is 20 + 5 = 25.

feedback.empty: Start with 1 × 5 and type the answer with the buttons.
feedback.not-finished: Keep going! The table isn't finished yet.
feedback.too-few: A few were wrong the first time. Press "Play again" and say the table once more.

two-five-ten.title: Times 2, 5 and 10
two-five-ten.prompt: 10 questions from the 2, 5 and 10 times tables. Quick, but no rush! Look at the picture if you need to.
two-five-ten.hint: Times 10: the digits move up a place (8 × 10 = 80). Times 5: half of times 10. Times 2: double the number.
two-five-ten.success: Great! You know your 2, 5 and 10 times tables.
two-five-ten.why: If you know 10 × 8 = 80, how can you find 5 × 8? Why does that work?
two-five-ten.model: 5 rows are half of 10 rows. So 5 × 8 is half of 10 × 8: half of 80 is 40.

feedback.empty: Answer the question first: type it with the buttons and press ✓.
feedback.not-finished: Keep going! There are a few questions left.
feedback.too-few: Fewer than 8 were right the first time this round. Press "Play again": the facts you missed come first.

zero-and-one.title: Times 0 and times 1
zero-and-one.prompt: Look at the pictures. 7 × 1 is 7 rows of 1. 7 × 0 is 7 empty rows! Now answer.
zero-and-one.hint: If one number is 0, there is nothing to count. If one number is 1, the answer is the other number.
zero-and-one.success: Well done! You found the rules for 0 and 1.
zero-and-one.why: Why is 9 × 0 equal to 0, but 9 + 0 equal to 9?
zero-and-one.model: 9 + 0 means you have 9 and add nothing, so you still have 9. 9 × 0 means 9 rows with nothing in each, so altogether you have nothing: 0.

feedback.not-finished: Keep going! There are a few questions left.
feedback.too-few: Play another round and look closely at the pictures: how many dots are in an empty row?

split-six-sevens.title: 6 × 7 from facts you know
split-six-sevens.prompt: This picture is 6 rows of 7. Move the line up and down to split it into two facts you know. Then type what 6 × 7 is.
split-six-sevens.hint: Put the line under 5 rows: 5 × 7 = 35, and one more row of 7. Or put it in the middle: two lots of 3 × 7.
split-six-sevens.why: How did 5 × 7 help you find 6 × 7? Why does that work?
split-six-sevens.model: 6 rows of 7 is 5 rows of 7 and one more row of 7. 5 × 7 = 35, then add one more 7: 35 + 7 = 42. No dots are lost; we only cut the picture into two parts.

feedback.empty: Type your answer in the box.
feedback.added: You added 6 and 7. But the picture is 6 rows of 7: count all the rows.
feedback.one-more-row: That's one row of 7 too many. 5 × 7 and one more row makes only 6 rows.
feedback.one-less-row: That is 5 × 7. There is one more row of 7 to add!
feedback.near: So close! Each row has 7 dots, not 6 or 8. Try again.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Put the line under 5 rows and work out the two parts separately.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Put the line under 5 rows and work out the two parts separately.

the-rest.title: The rest of the tables
the-rest.prompt: 12 questions from the 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12 times tables. If you don't know a fact, use one you do know. Turn on the gentle timer ⏱ if you like.
the-rest.hint: Double: 4 × 7 is double 2 × 7. Near ten: 9 × 6 is 10 × 6 take away one 6. Times 11 and 12: 10 lots, then 1 or 2 more lots.
the-rest.success: Well done! You know your times tables.
the-rest.why: Find 9 × 6 using 10 × 6. Why does that work?
the-rest.model: 9 rows of 6 is 10 rows of 6 take away one row. 10 × 6 = 60, then take away one 6: 60 − 6 = 54. So 9 × 6 = 54.

feedback.not-finished: Keep going! There are a few questions left.
feedback.too-few: Fewer than 10 were right the first time this round. Press "Play again": the facts you missed come first.
